content: The recommended dosage is 1 to 6 suppositories per day, administered rectally as needed. Stool softeners or bulk-forming laxatives may be used in combination with the suppository to enhance its effectiveness. However, the safety and efficacy of this treatment have not been firmly established. For hemorrhoids, the same dosage of 1 to 6 suppositories per day, rectally as needed, is advised. Stool softeners or bulk-forming laxatives can also be used alongside the suppository in this case. Patients should be aware of potential adverse effects, including irritation, pruritus (itching), or hypersensitivity to any of the ingredients in the suppository. If rectal bleeding occurs or the condition worsens after 7 days of use, the treatment should be re-evaluated by a healthcare professional. Regarding pregnancy, the medication falls under Category NA, meaning there is insufficient data to classify its safety during pregnancy. For lactation, it is not known whether the medication is excreted in breast milk. For medications classified as Category A, they are generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy. Controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk.
